title: How Many Pixels Is a Digit Worth? Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy for GUI Agent Confidence Estimation

paper.title: How Many Pixels Is a Digit Worth? Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy for GUI Agent Confidence Estimation
paper.abstract:
Abstract GUI agents predict click coordinates as digit-token sequences, but standard text-LLM confidence estimation methods rank correct clicks from wrong ones only weakly.
GUI-specific alternatives use K K samples or new supervision, but still leave room for improvement. We trace part of this to place-value asymmetry : bounding-
box correctness often makes higher-place digits more important than lower-place digits, so uniform aggregation weakens the signal that determines correctness. The
fix is to weight each digit’s Shannon entropy by its place value. We call this Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy (PACE). Across fixed-scale agents on
ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v 2 2 , PACE wins both AUROC and selective accuracy on all primary comparisons in a single forward pass, matching or outperforming K K -sample baselines at a fraction of the cost. PACE provides a per-click confidence estimate that turns coordinate-token internals into a practical confidence
signal for GUI agent deployment.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Figure 1: Place-value asymmetry on two real EvoCUA- 8 8 B predictions (Stata, ScreenSpot-Pro). (a) A correct click whose entropy lives in the units digit ( H = 2.29 H{=}2.29 , near-uniform over ten candidates 1 1 pixel apart) while the hundreds digit is locked ( H = 0.19 H{=}0.19 ). (b) A wrong click whose entropy lives in the hundreds digit ( H = 2.06 H{=}2.06 , five candidates 100 100 pixels apart) while the units digit is locked ( H = 0.27 H{=}0.27 ). Both cases share P(True) = 0.98 {=}0.98 . Coordinate-Entropy averages uniformly and ranks the correct click as more uncertain ( 1.41 > 0.92 1.41{>}0.92 ). PACE weights by place value and recovers the correct ranking ( 0.35 < 1.90 0.35{<}1.90 ). Open-source GUI agents predict pixel coordinates of clicks, keypresses, and scrolls from screenshots, driving professional desktop tasks end-to-end ( Qin et al., 2025 ; Xue et al., 2026 ; Hong et al., 2024 ; Xu et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2024 ) . Click accuracy on dense professional interfaces remains below half for the strongest open agents ( 35 35 – 50 % 50\% on ScreenSpot-Pro ( Li et al., 2025 ) ), and a wrong click is often irreversible: a sent payment or a deleted file cannot be undone by resampling ( Shi et al., 2025 ) . To manage this risk, the grounding model must therefore expose a per-prediction confidence estimate that ranks correct clicks above incorrect ones, and ideally produces a calibrated probability for downstream decisions. The same estimate can guide when the agent should act, ask for help, or use extra computation, and can be combined across steps in longer tasks. For ordinary text generation, confidence estimation is a mature toolkit. Verbalized prompts ( Tian et al., 2023 ; Kadavath et al., 2022 ) , self-consistency over multiple samples ( Wang et al., 2023 ) , and log-probability ( Malinin and Gales, 2021 ) all give usable confidence signals on factual question answering, semantic parsing, and reasoning traces. GUI click prediction also generates its output token by token: the model outputs a short digit-token sequence that decodes to screen coordinates. We find that these signals often provide weak or inconsistent discrimination for coordinate outputs (Table 1 ). We trace part of this to a common mechanism. GUI click correctness is bounding-box-defined: any pixel inside the target counts as correct. The hundreds digit of a coordinate therefore corresponds to larger, often UI-element-level shifts (a 1 1 -unit confusion is a 100 100 -pixel error that can land on a neighbor), while the units digit moves the click by only 1 1 pixel and is more likely to remain inside the same target. Per-token uncertainty is therefore asymmetric in its effect: entropy at higher-place digits is generally more informative for correctness, although lower-place digits still matter in some cases. Common token-level confidence signals aggregate uniformly across this asymmetric sequence, weakening the signal related to correctness. We call this property place-value asymmetry : per-position information content of a coordinate token sequence is non-uniform. We therefore scale each per-digit Shannon entropy by its place value before averaging. We call this Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy (PACE), parameterized by a single exponent α \alpha on the place value. For a 3-digit coordinate at α = 1 \alpha{=}1 , the hundred digit’s entropy contributes 100 × 100\times more than the unit digit’s to the score, matching the expected pixel cost of a one-digit error at each place; α = 0 \alpha{=}0 reduces to a uniform Coordinate-Entropy baseline. Unlike concurrent GUI confidence estimation methods that sample K K stochastic predictions (SafeGround ( Wang et al., 2026 ) ), train an extra verbalized head (HyperClick ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) ), or reduce the coordinate distribution to a point statistic (Peak Sharpness Score ( Tao et al., 2025 ) ), PACE reads only per-token entropies the model already computes during greedy decoding, so it requires no training, no architectural change, and no extra forward pass. We evaluate PACE on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v 2 2 ( Wu et al., 2024 ) across 7 7 open GUI agents, comparing against 12 12 single-pass and sampling-based confidence baselines on three primary agents. PACE α=1 wins both AUROC and selective accuracy on all 6 6 primary cells in a single forward pass, ahead of K K -sample baselines that pay an order of magnitude more in inference, and generally improves uniform Coordinate-Entropy along the full coverage–accuracy curve. We further study how much of the gain comes from using coordinate-token entropy and how much comes from place-value weighting, and discuss a quantile-based rule for downstream abstention. Our contributions are: • We identify place-value asymmetry in coordinate-token sequences and propose PACE , a parameter-free, training-free confidence signal that weights each digit’s entropy by its place value. • Across fixed-scale agents on two benchmarks, PACE achieves the best AUROC and AUARC in all primary comparisons in a single forward pass and generally improves uniform Coordinate-Entropy across the broader evaluation. • We analyze where the gain comes from by comparing full-sequence entropy, uniform Coordinate-Entropy, and PACE, separating the benefit of using coordinate tokens from the benefit of place-value weighting.

sections.heading: GUI agents and grounding benchmarks.
sections.text: Open GUI agents have scaled across multiple generations: from grounding-focused vision-language checkpoints ( Hong et al., 2024 ; Cheng et al., 2024 ) , through action-supervised trajectory-trained models ( Wu et al., 2024 ; Lin et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2025 ; Qin et al., 2025 ) , to recent state-of-the-art checkpoints on professional desktop tasks ( Xue et al., 2026 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ) . Closed-API prompted agents ( Zheng et al., 2024 ) sit alongside these as a parallel paradigm. Benchmarks have scaled from consumer UIs ( Wu et al., 2024 ) to professional UIs ( Li et al., 2025 ) and full-trajectory tasks ( Xie et al., 2024 ; Rawles et al., 2025 ) . Yet evaluation focuses on grounding accuracy or step success; per-prediction confidence remains an open channel, and the Trustworthy GUI Agents survey ( Shi et al., 2025 ) catalogues the safety gap.

sections.heading: GUI-specific confidence estimation.
sections.text: Concurrent GUI-specific confidence estimation falls along three lines. Peak Sharpness Score ( Tao et al., 2025 ) reads a per-token point statistic at coordinate positions, discarding the rest of the distributional shape. SafeGround ( Wang et al., 2026 ) samples K K stochastic clicks at temperature T T and uses their spatial entropy as the uncertainty signal for the original greedy-decoded click, paying roughly an order of magnitude more in inference for the uncertainty estimate alone. HyperClick ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) trains a verbalized confidence head with auxiliary reward, requiring supervised retraining. PACE differs from all three: it reads full distribution shape at each coordinate-digit position rather than a point statistic, and runs in a single greedy pass with no sampling, training, or architectural change.

sections.heading: LLM confidence estimation and abstention.
sections.text: Text-LLM confidence estimation has matured along several lines: verbalized prompts that ask the model to self-report ( Tian et al., 2023 ; Kadavath et al., 2022 ) , sampling agreement over multiple decodes ( Wang et al., 2023 ) , self-revision distance ( Madaan et al., 2023 ) , semantic entropy that clusters samples by meaning ( Kuhn et al., 2023 ; Farquhar et al., 2024 ) , and post-hoc calibrators applied to model logits ( Guo et al., 2017 ; Xiong et al., 2024 ) . A recent abstention survey ( Wen et al., 2025 ) catalogues these methods on text-domain tasks, leaving pixel-grounding outside the surveyed scope. Concurrent agentic uncertainty work ( Zhang et al., 2026b ; Zhang et al., 2026a ) extends these primitives to trajectory- or task-level aggregation for autonomous agents; PACE supplies the per-action confidence that trajectory-level aggregators consume. PACE can also serve as a cheap upstream gate for sampling-based test-time scaling ( Snell et al., 2024 ) , deciding which inputs deserve K K -sample refinement.

sections.heading: 3.1 GUI Click Confidence Estimation as a Selective-Prediction Task
sections.text: A GUI grounding model is a function f f that maps a screenshot I I and a natural-language instruction ℓ \ell to a predicted on-screen click y ^ ∈ ℝ 2 \hat{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{2} encoded as a digit-token sequence in the model’s output vocabulary. The ground-truth target for an instance ( I , ℓ ) (I,\ell) is a bounding box B ⊆ ℝ 2 B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2} , and the binary correctness label is y = 1 [ y ^ ∈ B ] . y\;=\;\mathbf{1}\bigl[\hat{y}\in B\bigr]. (1) A confidence score is any scalar c : ( I , ℓ ) → ℝ c\colon(I,\ell)\to\mathbb{R} derived from the model’s forward pass that is intended to rank predicted clicks by their probability of being correct. We say a confidence score is useful when clicks with higher c c are more often correct (discrimination). We evaluate discrimination with AUROC and the selective-accuracy integral AUARC. The score c c should also be cheap to compute, ideally falling out of the same forward pass the model already runs to predict y ^ \hat{y} .

sections.heading: 3.2 Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy (PACE)
sections.text: Let z 1 , … , z L z_{1},\ldots,z_{L} be the logit vectors at the L L coordinate-token positions produced during the model’s greedy decode, p k = softmax ⁡ ( z k ) p_{k}=\mathrm{softmax}(z_{k}) the per-position categorical distribution over the vocabulary, and H ( p k ) = − ∑ v p k ( v ) log p k ( v ) H(p_{k})=-\sum_{v}p_{k}(v)\log p_{k}(v) the corresponding Shannon entropy. For an L L -digit coordinate string, position k k carries place value v k = 10 L − 1 − k v_{k}=10^{L-1-k} . We aggregate the per-position entropies as a weighted average, PACE α = − ∑ k = 1 L v k α ​ H ​ ( p k ) ∑ k = 1 L v k α , \text{PACE}_{\alpha}\;=\;-\,\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{L}v_{k}^{\alpha}\,H(p_{k})}{\sum_{k=1}^{L}v_{k}^{\alpha}}\,, (2) where the leading negation reorients the score so that larger means more confident. The exponent α ≥ 0 \alpha\geq 0 controls how aggressively place value scales the weights. At α = 1 \alpha{=}1 the hundreds digit carries 100 × 100\times the weight of the units digit, consistent with the expected pixel deviation of a one-digit error at that place. At α = 0 \alpha{=}0 all positions contribute equally, yielding our Coordinate-Entropy baseline. The α = 1 \alpha{=}1 choice has a natural pixel-cost interpretation. Under a stylized noise model in which a one-digit confusion at place k k shifts the coordinate by 10 L − 1 − k 10^{L-1-k} pixels, the expected pixel error contributed by entropy at position k k scales as 10 L − 1 − k ⋅ H ⁡ ( p k ) 10^{L-1-k}\cdot H(p_{k}) . Summing and normalizing recovers Equation 2 with α = 1 \alpha{=}1 . Entropy is not literally expected absolute pixel displacement, so this is a heuristic motivation rather than a first-principles derivation; we adopt α = 1 \alpha{=}1 as the simplest parameter-free weighting consistent with place-value asymmetry, and validate empirically (§ 5.2 ) that a data-driven linear fit recovers the same ordering. Implementation: greedy-decode the click, identify coordinate-digit positions in the output, then evaluate Equation 2 from the cached per-step logits. sections.heading: Datasets.
sections.text: ScreenSpot-Pro ( Li et al., 2025 ) provides 1,581 1{,}581 click-grounding tasks across 23 23 professional desktop applications such as Photoshop, AutoCAD, and MATLAB. ScreenSpot-v 2 2 ( Wu et al., 2024 ) provides 1,272 1{,}272 click-grounding tasks across consumer mobile, web, and desktop UIs. Each task is an (instruction, screenshot, target bounding box) triple; the agent’s predicted click is scored correct if it falls inside the target box.

sections.heading: Models.
sections.text: The three primary agents are EvoCUA- 8 8 B ( Xue et al., 2026 ) , MAI-UI- 8 8 B ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) , and UGround-V 1 1 - 7 7 B ( Gou et al., 2025 ) . Four additional agents (UGround-V 1 1 - 2 2 B, UI-TARS- 7 7 B-SFT, UI-TARS- 7 7 B-DPO ( Qin et al., 2025 ) , Aguvis- 7 7 B-720P ( Xu et al., 2025 ) ) support the cross-agent paired analysis.

sections.heading: Confidence estimation baselines.
sections.text: We compare PACE against 12 12 baselines in four categories, ordered to match Table 1 . Verbalized signals query the model directly: Self-Refine ( Madaan et al., 2023 ) runs one round of self-critique before re-prompting for confidence; Just Ask 1 1 – 10 10 ( Tian et al., 2023 ) returns an integer on a 1 1 to 10 10 scale; P(True) ( Kadavath et al., 2022 ) asks an A/B correctness question and reads the softmax probability of “A”. Full-sequence signals (logit-min, logit-mean, full-sequence Shannon entropy) aggregate over every output token, coordinate-digit and surface-form alike. Sampling-based signals draw K = 10 K{=}10 samples at temperature T = 1.0 T{=}1.0 : SafeGround entropy is the density entropy over the K K predicted click positions, and SafeGround combined ( Wang et al., 2026 ) adds patch-level disagreement on top. Coordinate-token signals read only the coordinate-digit positions: coordinate max-entropy, the worst-position entropy; PSS ( Tao et al., 2025 ) , the top- 1 1 /top- 2 2 logit margin at each position; coordinate mean top- 1 1 probability (the average greedy-token softmax probability across coordinate positions); and Coordinate-Entropy (PACE α=0 , the uniform-weight baseline).

sections.heading: Metrics.
sections.text: AUROC ranks correct against incorrect clicks by confidence score. AUARC is the selective-accuracy integral: how much accuracy the agent retains when allowed to abstain on its lowest-confidence fraction. All signals are evaluated on the same greedy clicks; sampling-based methods use their samples only to estimate uncertainty.

sections.heading: Comparisons with baselines.
sections.text: Table 1 compares PACE with twelve confidence baselines from four families across the three primary agents. PACE α=1 achieves the highest AUROC and AUARC on all three agents using a single forward pass, outperforming sampling baselines that use K = 10 K{=}10 stochastic decodes per decision. Across the three agents, PACE reaches 87 87 – 91 % 91\% of the perfect-ranking AUARC ceiling, leaving a relatively small absolute gap to the oracle ranking on this metric.

sections.heading: Decomposing the gain.
sections.text: The PACE α=1 advantage comes from two components. First, Shannon entropy at coordinate-digit positions alone (Coordinate-Entropy) already outperforms the strongest alternative single-pass summaries by 0.02 0.02 – 0.08 0.08 mean AUROC across the three primary agents. The reason is distributional: these summaries retain only part of the predictive distribution. PSS uses only the top-two logit gap, the mean top-one probability uses only the greedy-token probability at each coordinate position, and max-entropy uses only the worst position. When uncertainty is spread across several digit candidates, these summaries can miss part of the distributional structure; Shannon entropy instead uses the full categorical distribution at each position. Second, place-value weighting adds 0.022 0.022 mean AUROC over Coordinate-Entropy, with positive gains on all three primary agents.

sections.heading: Response-level confidence can differ from click accuracy.
sections.text: The ranking metrics above measure whether a confidence score orders correct and incorrect clicks. We separately examine how the standard logit-mean score relates to task accuracy, where Conf is the per-token top-1 softmax probability averaged across the response. For MAI-UI-8B and EvoCUA-8B, logit-mean confidence remains high on ScreenSpot-Pro even though click accuracy is much lower. On ScreenSpot-v2, both confidence and accuracy are high (Table 2 ). These results show that averaging confidence over the full response can hide uncertainty concentrated in the coordinate digits that determine the click. This motivates a coordinate-local signal. PACE reads entropy at those positions and is evaluated as a ranking signal rather than a calibrated probability. sections.heading: 5.1 Why PACE Works: Hundreds Digit Carries the Signal
sections.text: A one-digit confusion at the hundreds place (for example x = 502 x{=}502 vs. x = 602 x{=}602 ) changes the normalized coordinate by 100 100 grid units and can move the click onto a neighboring UI element. The same confusion at the units place ( x = 502 x{=}502 vs. x = 508 x{=}508 ) changes the coordinate by only 6 6 grid units and is more likely to remain inside the target. Per-position uncertainty is therefore not interchangeable: hundreds-digit uncertainty is more predictive of incorrect clicks than units-digit uncertainty. When averaged across agents, single-digit entropy AUROC increases from fine to coarse places (Figure 2 a ), from 0.65 0.65 at units to 0.77 0.77 at tens and 0.82 0.82 at hundreds. The expected entropy gap 𝔼 ⁡ [ H ∣ wrong ] − 𝔼 ⁡ [ H ∣ correct ] \mathbb{E}[H\mid\mathrm{wrong}]-\mathbb{E}[H\mid\mathrm{correct}] follows the same pattern (Figure 2 b ). PACE α=1 assigns roughly 90 % 90\% of its positional weight to the hundreds digit, where the empirical signal is strongest. Figure 2: Per-place informativeness justifies place-weighting. (a) Single-digit AUROC at each digit place; family mean rises monotonically units to hundreds. (b) Per-place entropy gap between wrong and correct predictions tracks the same gradient.

sections.heading: 5.3 Visualizing Signal Quality
sections.text: Figure 3 contrasts the EvoCUA- 8 8 B confidence distributions of three signal families on ScreenSpot-Pro: PACE α=1 , confidence derived from full-sequence probability, and verbalized P(True). PACE shows the clearest separation between correct (green) and incorrect (red) clicks, while full- sequence probability provides only partial separation. The P(True) distributions overlap substantially, consistent with its below-chance AUROC in this setting. These distributions help explain the selective-prediction results: PACE provides a more useful confidence threshold for deciding whether to execute a click or hand it off, whereas P(True) offers little separation for that decision. Appendix C analyzes the corresponding limitations of full-sequence aggregation, verbalized confidence, and self-consistency. Figure 3: Confidence distributions on EvoCUA- 8 8 B ScreenSpot-Pro. sections.heading: 5.4 Downstream: Selective Prediction and Abstention

Selective prediction ( Geifman and El-Yaniv, 2017 ) evaluates this decision through the accuracy of executed clicks at different coverage levels. On the five-agent mean, PACE α=1 outperforms Coordinate-Entropy at every coverage level reported in Table 6 . The difference is largest at low coverage, where the agent executes only its highest-confidence clicks and abstains on the rest. At 5 % 5\% coverage, PACE raises mean selective accuracy from 63.8 % 63.8\% to 73.2 % 73.2\% . sections.heading: Wrong-click prevention.
sections.text: Table 7 reports representative abstention settings for EvoCUA- 8 8 B. PACE α=1 removes at least as many wrong clicks as Coordinate-Entropy on ScreenSpot-Pro and substantially more on ScreenSpot-v 2 2 . These results complement selective accuracy by showing directly how often confidence-based abstention prevents an incorrect click from being executed. sections.heading: 6 Conclusion
sections.text: GUI agents often emit clicks as short digit-token sequences on a fixed coordinate grid. Standard text-LLM confidence methods aggregate across tokens or coordinate positions without accounting for place value asymmetry. Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy addresses this mismatch by computing Shannon entropy at coordinate- token positions and weighting each digit by its decimal place value. The resulting confidence score requires only the logits from a single greedy decode. Across the three primary agents, PACE α=1 achieves the best AUROC and AUARC in all six agent and metric comparisons. In the eight-agent comparison, place weighting improves mean AUROC on both ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v 2 2 , including a positive result for a 72 72 B fixed-scale model. PACE also supports a direct execution decision: the agent executes high-confidence clicks and abstains on low-confidence ones. Across the evaluated fixed-scale agents, PACE prevents more wrong clicks than Coordinate-Entropy at most reported abstention settings, with its largest gains appearing at low coverage. These results connect the ranking improvement to fewer incorrect clicks being executed. The evidence is scoped to coordinate formats with separately tokenized digits and a stable place-value map. For variable-scale pixel coordinates, fractional outputs, or merged digit tokens, decimal place weighting is not guaranteed to help, and Coordinate-Entropy remains the appropriate fallback. One possible future work is to explore how PACE can guide abstention and recovery decisions in closed-loop, multi-step GUI agents.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.text: • Closed-loop interaction. Our main evaluation focuses on individual grounding decisions on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v 2 2 . It does not establish how confidence-based abstention affects long-horizon task completion. Future work should evaluate PACE in closed-loop, multi-step GUI agents. • Emission format. PACE assumes that coordinates are emitted as separately tokenized digits on a stable scale. Decimal place weighting is not guaranteed to help with variable-scale pixel coordinates, fractional outputs, or merged digit tokens; Coordinate-Entropy is the appropriate fallback in these settings. • Model coverage. Although our evaluation spans models from 2 2 B to 72 72 B, the large-scale evidence comes from a single 72 72 B fixed-scale agent. Additional large and proprietary agents are needed to separate the effects of model scale, architecture, and coordinate format. • Discrimination, not probability calibration. PACE is designed to rank clicks by confidence rather than estimate their probability of correctness. It can be thresholded directly for abstention, but applications that require calibrated error probabilities need a separate post-hoc calibration procedure.

sections.heading: Ethical Considerations
sections.text: GUI agents operate on interfaces whose actions are not always reversible ( Shi et al., 2025 ) ; the cost of a misgrounded click extends beyond the immediate task. PACE is a per-step uncertainty primitive for downstream safeguards (clarification, human review, abstention, escalation), not a standalone deployment certificate. Safety-critical deployment should include per-application monitoring, recomputation of the calibration set under distribution shift, and clear allocation of responsibility between the automated decision and human oversight.

sections.heading: Coordinate-token identification.
sections.text: For structured tool calls, we locate the coordinate field and align its decoded characters with the corresponding generation steps. We retain only tokens that emit a single decimal digit and parse the x x and y y axes separately. A prediction enters the fixed-three-digit analysis only when both axes contain exactly three such digit tokens. Tokens that merge multiple digits do not provide a valid place map and therefore fall back to Coordinate-Entropy.

sections.heading: Appendix C Structural Properties: Coordinate vs. Full-Sequence Tokens
sections.text: Coordinate-Entropy outperforms full-sequence logit summaries because the two approaches aggregate uncertainty from different parts of the response.

sections.heading: Action relevance.
sections.text: Full responses contain reasoning, formatting, and tool-call tokens whose variation does not necessarily change the predicted click. Coordinate tokens are more directly tied to the executed action because changing a coordinate digit changes the predicted location. Although multiple coordinates within a target box may be correct, uncertainty at coordinate positions is therefore more closely related to click correctness than uncertainty in surrounding response tokens.

sections.heading: Dilution under full-sequence aggregation.
sections.text: Full-sequence summaries average coordinate uncertainty together with uncertainty from the rest of the response, which can dilute the signal associated with the predicted location. In contrast, Coordinate-Entropy evaluates only the tokens that determine the click. The strong performance of coordinate-level entropy and the coordinate-level top-two logit gap in Table 1 is consistent with this explanation.

Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy for GUI Agent Confidence Estimation Yunxiang Li Affiliation: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China Email: yli@se.cuhk.edu.hk Xixin Wu Affiliation: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China Helen Meng † † thanks: $ $Corresponding author. Affiliation: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China Abstract GUI agents predict click coordinates as digit-token sequences, but standard text-LLM confidence estimation methods rank correct clicks from wrong ones only weakly. GUI-specific alternatives use K K samples or new supervision, but still leave room for improvement. We trace part of this to place-value asymmetry : bounding- box correctness often makes higher-place digits more important than lower-place digits, so uniform aggregation weakens the signal that determines correctness. The fix is to weight each digit’s Shannon entropy by its place value. We call this Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy (PACE). Across fixed-scale agents on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v 2 2 , PACE wins both AUROC and selective accuracy on all primary comparisons in a single forward pass, matching or outperforming K K -sample baselines at a fraction of the cost. PACE provides a per-click confidence estimate that turns coordinate-token internals into a practical confidence signal for GUI agent deployment. 1 Introduction Figure 1: Place-value asymmetry on two real EvoCUA- 8 8 B predictions (Stata, ScreenSpot-Pro). (a) A correct click whose entropy lives in the units digit ( H = 2.29 H{=}2.29 , near-uniform over ten candidates 1 1 pixel apart) while the hundreds digit is locked ( H = 0.19 H{=}0.19 ). (b) A wrong click whose entropy lives in the hundreds digit ( H = 2.06 H{=}2.06 , five candidates 100 100 pixels apart) while the units digit is locked ( H = 0.27 H{=}0.27 ). Both cases share P(True) = 0.98 {=}0.98 . Coordinate-Entropy averages uniformly and ranks the correct click as more uncertain ( 1.41 > 0.92 1.41{>}0.92 ). PACE weights by place value and recovers the correct ranking ( 0.35 < 1.90 0.35{<}1.90 ). Open-source GUI agents predict pixel coordinates of clicks, keypresses, and scrolls from screenshots, driving professional desktop tasks end-to-end ( Qin et al., 2025 ; Xue et al., 2026 ; Hong et al., 2024 ; Xu et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2024 ) . Click accuracy on dense professional interfaces remains below half for the strongest open agents ( 35 35 – 50 % 50\% on ScreenSpot-Pro ( Li et al., 2025 ) ), and a wrong click is often irreversible: a sent payment or a deleted file cannot be undone by resampling ( Shi et al., 2025 ) . To manage this risk, the grounding model must therefore expose a per-prediction confidence estimate that ranks correct clicks above incorrect ones, and ideally produces a calibrated probability for downstream decisions. The same estimate can guide when the agent should act, ask for help, or use extra computation, and can be combined across steps in longer tasks. For ordinary text generation, confidence estimation is a mature toolkit. Verbalized prompts ( Tian et al., 2023 ; Kadavath et al., 2022 ) , self-consistency over multiple samples ( Wang et al., 2023 ) , and log-probability ( Malinin and Gales, 2021 ) all give usable confidence signals on factual question answering, semantic parsing, and reasoning traces. GUI click prediction also generates its output token by token: the model outputs a short digit-token sequence that decodes to screen coordinates. We find that these signals often provide weak or inconsistent discrimination for coordinate outputs (Table 1 ). We trace part of this to a common mechanism. GUI click correctness is bounding-box-defined: any pixel inside the target counts as correct. The hundreds digit of a coordinate therefore corresponds to larger, often UI-element-level shifts (a 1 1 -unit confusion is a 100 100 -pixel error that can land on a neighbor), while the units digit moves the click by only 1 1 pixel and is more likely to remain inside the same target. Per-token uncertainty is therefore asymmetric in its effect: entropy at higher-place digits is generally more informative for correctness, although lower-place digits still matter in some cases. Common token-level confidence signals aggregate uniformly across this asymmetric sequence, weakening the signal related to correctness. We call this property place-value asymmetry : per-position information content of a coordinate token sequence is non-uniform. We therefore scale each per-digit Shannon entropy by its place value before averaging. We call this Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy (PACE), parameterized by a single exponent α \alpha on the place value. For a 3-digit coordinate at α = 1 \alpha{=}1 , the hundred digit’s entropy contributes 100 × 100\times more than the unit digit’s to the score, matching the expected pixel cost of a one-digit error at each place; α = 0 \alpha{=}0 reduces to a uniform Coordinate-Entropy baseline. Unlike concurrent GUI confidence estimation methods that sample K K stochastic predictions (SafeGround ( Wang et al., 2026 ) ), train an extra verbalized head (HyperClick ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) ), or reduce the coordinate distribution to a point statistic (Peak Sharpness Score ( Tao et al., 2025 ) ), PACE reads only per-token entropies the model already computes during greedy decoding, so it requires no training, no architectural change, and no extra forward pass. We evaluate PACE on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v 2 2 ( Wu et al., 2024 ) across 7 7 open GUI agents, comparing against 12 12 single-pass and sampling-based confidence baselines on three primary agents. PACE α=1 wins both AUROC and selective accuracy on all 6 6 primary cells in a single forward pass, ahead of K K -sample baselines that pay an order of magnitude more in inference, and generally improves uniform Coordinate-Entropy along the full coverage–accuracy curve. We further study how much of the gain comes from using coordinate-token entropy and how much comes from place-value weighting, and discuss a quantile-based rule for downstream abstention. Our contributions are: • We identify place-value asymmetry in coordinate-token sequences and propose PACE , a parameter-free, training-free confidence signal that weights each digit’s entropy by its place value. • Across fixed-scale agents on two benchmarks, PACE achieves the best AUROC and AUARC in all primary comparisons in a single forward pass and generally improves uniform Coordinate-Entropy across the broader evaluation. • We analyze where the gain comes from by comparing full-sequence entropy, uniform Coordinate-Entropy, and PACE, separating the benefit of using coordinate tokens from the benefit of place-value weighting. 2 Related Work GUI agents and grounding benchmarks. Open GUI agents have scaled across multiple generations: from grounding-focused vision-language checkpoints ( Hong et al., 2024 ; Cheng et al., 2024 ) , through action-supervised trajectory-trained models ( Wu et al., 2024 ; Lin et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2025 ; Qin et al., 2025 ) , to recent state-of-the-art checkpoints on professional desktop tasks ( Xue et al., 2026 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ) . Closed-API prompted agents ( Zheng et al., 2024 ) sit alongside these as a parallel paradigm. Benchmarks have scaled from consumer UIs ( Wu et al., 2024 ) to professional UIs ( Li et al., 2025 ) and full-trajectory tasks ( Xie et al., 2024 ; Rawles et al., 2025 ) . Yet evaluation focuses on grounding accuracy or step success; per-prediction confidence remains an open channel, and the Trustworthy GUI Agents survey ( Shi et al., 2025 ) catalogues the safety gap. GUI-specific confidence estimation. Concurrent GUI-specific confidence estimation falls along three lines. Peak Sharpness Score ( Tao et al., 2025 ) reads a per-token point statistic at coordinate positions, discarding the rest of the distributional shape. SafeGround ( Wang et al., 2026 ) samples K K stochastic clicks at temperature T T and uses their spatial entropy as the uncertainty signal for the original greedy-decoded click, paying roughly an order of magnitude more in inference for the uncertainty estimate alone. HyperClick ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) trains a verbalized confidence head with auxiliary reward, requiring supervised retraining. PACE differs from all three: it reads full distribution shape at each coordinate-digit position rather than a point statistic, and runs in a single greedy pass with no sampling, training, or architectural change. LLM confidence estimation and abstention. Text-LLM confidence estimation has matured along several lines: verbalized prompts that ask the model to self-report ( Tian et al., 2023 ; Kadavath et al., 2022 ) , sampling agreement over multiple decodes ( Wang et al., 2023 ) , self-revision distance ( Madaan et al., 2023 ) , semantic entropy that clusters samples by meaning ( Kuhn et al., 2023 ; Farquhar et al., 2024 ) , and post-hoc calibrators applied to model logits ( Guo et al., 2017 ; Xiong et al., 2024 ) . A recent abstention survey ( Wen et al., 2025 ) catalogues these methods on text-domain tasks, leaving pixel-grounding outside the surveyed scope. Concurrent agentic uncertainty work ( Zhang et al., 2026b ; Zhang et al., 2026a ) extends these primitives to trajectory- or task-level aggregation for autonomous agents; PACE supplies the per-action confidence that trajectory-level aggregators consume. PACE can also serve as a cheap upstream gate for sampling-based test-time scaling ( Snell et al., 2024 ) , deciding which inputs deserve K K -sample refinement. 3 Method 3.1 GUI Click Confidence Estimation as a Selective-Prediction Task A GUI grounding model is a function f f that maps a screenshot I I and a natural-language instruction ℓ \ell to a predicted on-screen click y ^ ∈ ℝ 2 \hat{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{2} encoded as a digit-token sequence in the model’s output vocabulary. The ground-truth target for an instance ( I , ℓ ) (I,\ell) is a bounding box B ⊆ ℝ 2 B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2} , and the binary correctness label is y = 1 [ y ^ ∈ B ] . y\;=\;\mathbf{1}\bigl[\hat{y}\in B\bigr]. (1) A confidence score is any scalar c : ( I , ℓ ) → ℝ c\colon(I,\ell)\to\mathbb{R} derived from the model’s forward pass that is intended to rank predicted clicks by their probability of being correct. We say a confidence score is useful when clicks with higher c c are more often correct (discrimination). We evaluate discrimination with AUROC and the selective-accuracy integral AUARC. The score c c should also be cheap to compute, ideally falling out of the same forward pass the model already runs to predict y ^ \hat{y} . 3.2 Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy (PACE) Let z 1 , … , z L z_{1},\ldots,z_{L} be the logit vectors at the L L coordinate-token positions produced during the model’s greedy decode, p k = softmax ⁡ ( z k ) p_{k}=\mathrm{softmax}(z_{k}) the per-position categorical distribution over the vocabulary, and H ( p k ) = − ∑ v p k ( v ) log p k ( v ) H(p_{k})=-\sum_{v}p_{k}(v)\log p_{k}(v) the corresponding Shannon entropy. For an L L -digit coordinate string, position k k carries place value v k = 10 L − 1 − k v_{k}=10^{L-1-k} . We aggregate the per-position entropies as a weighted average, PACE α = − ∑ k = 1 L v k α ​ H ​ ( p k ) ∑ k = 1 L v k α , \text{PACE}_{\alpha}\;=\;-\,\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{L}v_{k}^{\alpha}\,H(p_{k})}{\sum_{k=1}^{L}v_{k}^{\alpha}}\,, (2) where the leading negation reorients the score so that larger means more confident. The exponent α ≥ 0 \alpha\geq 0 controls how aggressively place value scales the weights. At α = 1 \alpha{=}1 the hundreds digit carries 100 × 100\times the weight of the units digit, consistent with the expected pixel deviation of a one-digit error at that place. At α = 0 \alpha{=}0 all positions contribute equally, yielding our Coordinate-Entropy baseline. The α = 1 \alpha{=}1 choice has a natural pixel-cost interpretation. Under a stylized noise model in which a one-digit confusion at place k k shifts the coordinate by 10 L − 1 − k 10^{L-1-k} pixels, the expected pixel error contributed by entropy at position k k scales as 10 L − 1 − k ⋅ H ⁡ ( p k ) 10^{L-1-k}\cdot H(p_{k}) . Summing and normalizing recovers Equation 2 with α = 1 \alpha{=}1 . Entropy is not literally expected absolute pixel displacement, so this is a heuristic motivation rather than a first-principles derivation; we adopt α = 1 \alpha{=}1 as the simplest parameter-free weighting consistent with place-value asymmetry, and validate empirically (§ 5.2 ) that a data-driven linear fit recovers the same ordering. Implementation: greedy-decode the click, identify coordinate-digit positions in the output, then evaluate Equation 2 from the cached per-step logits. ScreenSpot-Pro ( Li et al., 2025 ) provides 1,581 1{,}581 click-grounding tasks across 23 23 professional desktop applications such as Photoshop, AutoCAD, and MATLAB. ScreenSpot-v 2 2 ( Wu et al., 2024 ) provides 1,272 1{,}272 click-grounding tasks across consumer mobile, web, and desktop UIs. Each task is an (instruction, screenshot, target bounding box) triple; the agent’s predicted click is scored correct if it falls inside the target box. Models. The three primary agents are EvoCUA- 8 8 B ( Xue et al., 2026 ) , MAI-UI- 8 8 B ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) , and UGround-V 1 1 - 7 7 B ( Gou et al., 2025 ) . Four additional agents (UGround-V 1 1 - 2 2 B, UI-TARS- 7 7 B-SFT, UI-TARS- 7 7 B-DPO ( Qin et al., 2025 ) , Aguvis- 7 7 B-720P ( Xu et al., 2025 ) ) support the cross-agent paired analysis. Confidence estimation baselines. We compare PACE against 12 12 baselines in four categories, ordered to match Table 1 . Verbalized signals query the model directly: Self-Refine ( Madaan et al., 2023 ) runs one round of self-critique before re-prompting for confidence; Just Ask 1 1 – 10 10 ( Tian et al., 2023 ) returns an integer on a 1 1 to 10 10 scale; P(True) ( Kadavath et al., 2022 ) asks an A/B correctness question and reads the softmax probability of “A”. Full-sequence signals (logit-min, logit-mean, full-sequence Shannon entropy) aggregate over every output token, coordinate-digit and surface-form alike. Sampling-based signals draw K = 10 K{=}10 samples at temperature T = 1.0 T{=}1.0 : SafeGround entropy is the density entropy over the K K predicted click positions, and SafeGround combined ( Wang et al., 2026 ) adds patch-level disagreement on top. Coordinate-token signals read only the coordinate-digit positions: coordinate max-entropy, the worst-position entropy; PSS ( Tao et al., 2025 ) , the top- 1 1 /top- 2 2 logit margin at each position; coordinate mean top- 1 1 probability (the average greedy-token softmax probability across coordinate positions); and Coordinate-Entropy (PACE α=0 , the uniform-weight baseline). Metrics. AUROC ranks correct against incorrect clicks by confidence score. AUARC is the selective-accuracy integral: how much accuracy the agent retains when allowed to abstain on its lowest-confidence fraction. All signals are evaluated on the same greedy clicks; sampling-based methods use their samples only to estimate uncertainty. 4.2 Main Results Comparisons with baselines. Table 1 compares PACE with twelve confidence baselines from four families across the three primary agents. PACE α=1 achieves the highest AUROC and AUARC on all three agents using a single forward pass, outperforming sampling baselines that use K = 10 K{=}10 stochastic decodes per decision. Across the three agents, PACE reaches 87 87 – 91 % 91\% of the perfect-ranking AUARC ceiling, leaving a relatively small absolute gap to the oracle ranking on this metric. Decomposing the gain. The PACE α=1 advantage comes from two components. First, Shannon entropy at coordinate-digit positions alone (Coordinate-Entropy) already outperforms the strongest alternative single-pass summaries by 0.02 0.02 – 0.08 0.08 mean AUROC across the three primary agents. The reason is distributional: these summaries retain only part of the predictive distribution. PSS uses only the top-two logit gap, the mean top-one probability uses only the greedy-token probability at each coordinate position, and max-entropy uses only the worst position. When uncertainty is spread across several digit candidates, these summaries can miss part of the distributional structure; Shannon entropy instead uses the full categorical distribution at each position. Second, place-value weighting adds 0.022 0.022 mean AUROC over Coordinate-Entropy, with positive gains on all three primary agents. Response-level confidence can differ from click accuracy. The ranking metrics above measure whether a confidence score orders correct and incorrect clicks. We separately examine how the standard logit-mean score relates to task accuracy, where Conf is the per-token top-1 softmax probability averaged across the response. For MAI-UI-8B and EvoCUA-8B, logit-mean confidence remains high on ScreenSpot-Pro even though click accuracy is much lower. On ScreenSpot-v2, both confidence and accuracy are high (Table 2 ). These results show that averaging confidence over the full response can hide uncertainty concentrated in the coordinate digits that determine the click. This motivates a coordinate-local signal. The same confusion at the units place ( x = 502 x{=}502 vs. x = 508 x{=}508 ) changes the coordinate by only 6 6 grid units and is more likely to remain inside the target. Per-position uncertainty is therefore not interchangeable: hundreds-digit uncertainty is more predictive of incorrect clicks than units-digit uncertainty. When averaged across agents, single-digit entropy AUROC increases from fine to coarse places (Figure 2 a ), from 0.65 0.65 at units to 0.77 0.77 at tens and 0.82 0.82 at hundreds. PACE shows the clearest separation between correct (green) and incorrect (red) clicks, while full- sequence probability provides only partial separation. The P(True) distributions overlap substantially, consistent with its below-chance AUROC in this setting. These distributions help explain the selective-prediction results: PACE provides a more useful confidence threshold for deciding whether to execute a click or hand it off, whereas P(True) offers little separation for that decision. AUROC values are shown within each panel. 5.4 Downstream: Selective Prediction and Abstention A deployed GUI agent does not act on a confidence ranking metric directly. It must decide for each click whether to execute it or abstain. Selective prediction ( Geifman and El-Yaniv, 2017 ) evaluates this decision through the accuracy of executed clicks at different coverage levels. On the five-agent mean, PACE α=1 outperforms Coordinate-Entropy at every coverage level reported in Table 6 . Standard text-LLM confidence methods aggregate across tokens or coordinate positions without accounting for place value asymmetry. Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy addresses this mismatch by computing Shannon entropy at coordinate- token positions and weighting each digit by its decimal place value. The resulting confidence score requires only the logits from a single greedy decode. Across the three primary agents, PACE α=1 achieves the best AUROC and AUARC in all six agent and metric comparisons. In the eight-agent comparison, place weighting improves mean AUROC on both ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v 2 2 , including a positive result for a 72 72 B fixed-scale model. PACE also supports a direct execution decision: the agent executes high-confidence clicks and abstains on low-confidence ones. Across the evaluated fixed-scale agents, PACE prevents more wrong clicks than Coordinate-Entropy at most reported abstention settings, with its largest gains appearing at low coverage. These results connect the ranking improvement to fewer incorrect clicks being executed. The evidence is scoped to coordinate formats with separately tokenized digits and a stable place-value map. For variable-scale pixel coordinates, fractional outputs, or merged digit tokens, decimal place weighting is not guaranteed to help, and Coordinate-Entropy remains the appropriate fallback. One possible future work is to explore how PACE can guide abstention and recovery decisions in closed-loop, multi-step GUI agents. Limitations • Closed-loop interaction. Our main evaluation focuses on individual grounding decisions on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v 2 2 . It does not establish how confidence-based abstention affects long-horizon task completion. Future work should evaluate PACE in closed-loop, multi-step GUI agents. • Emission format. PACE assumes that coordinates are emitted as separately tokenized digits on a stable scale. Decimal place weighting is not guaranteed to help with variable-scale pixel coordinates, fractional outputs, or merged digit tokens; Coordinate-Entropy is the appropriate fallback in these settings. • Model coverage. Although our evaluation spans models from 2 2 B to 72 72 B, the large-scale evidence comes from a single 72 72 B fixed-scale agent. Additional large and proprietary agents are needed to separate the effects of model scale, architecture, and coordinate format. • Discrimination, not probability calibration. PACE is designed to rank clicks by confidence rather than estimate their probability of correctness. It can be thresholded directly for abstention, but applications that require calibrated error probabilities need a separate post-hoc calibration procedure. Ethical Considerations GUI agents operate on interfaces whose actions are not always reversible ( Shi et al., 2025 ) ; the cost of a misgrounded click extends beyond the immediate task. PACE is a per-step uncertainty primitive for downstream safeguards (clarification, human review, abstention, escalation), not a standalone deployment certificate. Safety-critical deployment should include per-application monitoring, recomputation of the calibration set under distribution shift, and clear allocation of responsibility between the automated decision and human oversight. Appendix C Structural Properties: Coordinate vs. Full-Sequence Tokens Coordinate-Entropy outperforms full-sequence logit summaries because the two approaches aggregate uncertainty from different parts of the response. Action relevance. Full responses contain reasoning, formatting, and tool-call tokens whose variation does not necessarily change the predicted click. Coordinate tokens are more directly tied to the executed action because changing a coordinate digit changes the predicted location. Although multiple coordinates within a target box may be correct, uncertainty at coordinate positions is therefore more closely related to click correctness than uncertainty in surrounding response tokens. Dilution under full-sequence aggregation. Full-sequence summaries average coordinate uncertainty together with uncertainty from the rest of the response, which can dilute the signal associated with the predicted location. In contrast, Coordinate-Entropy evaluates only the tokens that determine the click. The strong performance of coordinate-level entropy and the coordinate-level top-two logit gap in Table 1 is consistent with this explanation.
